_schema: Diameter, pitch and blade count set the thrust and torque coefficients (physics.md §4: T = C_T*rho*n^2*D^4, Q = C_Q*rho*n^2*D^5). Thrust goes as D^4, so diameter dominates everything else on this list. Including both a 2-blade and a 3-blade at the same 5x4.3 is deliberate: it is the cleanest A/B in the catalog, because bi-blade is smoother and more efficient while tri-blade has more grip and draws more current. Two tiers, as in frames.json: `specs` is physics-bearing and `catalog` is browsing metadata only — a field is admitted to `catalog` only if it is a factual, checkable property of the real product AND is needed to navigate the catalog at scale. Colour, price and vendor links are banned by name from both blocks. Entries are ordered smallest diameter first, which is what gives the diameter filter an ascending order without anything sorting it. 'material' is browsing metadata rather than a spec because nothing in the physics reads it yet: blade stiffness would change the thrust curve, and the day this model grows a flex term is the day it moves into `specs`.

parts.name: Nazgul F5 5.1x3.5x3
parts.source: iFlight 'Nazgul F5 Tri-blade Prop' product page (shop.iflight.com, product 964): diameter 5.1 inch, pitch 3.5, 3 blades, 3.9 g each, polycarbonate, 5 mm centre hole. A NAMED PRODUCT rather than a class-typical entry, because it is the prop the held-out builds in data/validation/builds.json actually fly AND the prop iFlight's own XING2 2207 datasheet quotes a thrust row on — one prop, one source, both sides.

parts.name: HQProp Ethix S5 5x4x3
parts.source: GEPRC 'HQ Ethix S5 5X4X3 Propeller' product page (geprc.com/product/hq-ethix-s5-5x4x3-propeller/), Specifications block: 'Propeller Size: 5″', 'Pitch: 4″', 'Blades: 3', 'Material: Polycarbonate', 'Weight: 3.7g', 'Shaft: 5mm'. Here because it is the prop GEPRC's OWN SPEEDX2 2107.5 motor data table quotes the headline thrust row on — one vendor, one bench, both sides of the k_t fit — not because any validation aircraft flies it.
